Can you describe exactly where you feel the weakness and decreased sensation in your right arm, and when did these symptoms first start?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Weakness in the right arm. I also have Decreased sensation in the right arm, Dull aching and burning pain in the right arm, Significant weight loss. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Has the weakness been progressive over weeks or months, or did it start suddenly? Also, have you noticed any trouble with your speech, vision changes, or balance issues recently? REQUEST TEST: TSH (Thyroid Stimulating Hormone) and Request Images: MRI Cervical Spine.

speaker: Doctor
text: That's interesting—could you describe whether the weakness affects specific muscles (like grip strength) or if it's more generalized? Also, do you have any history of recent infections, fever, or neck trauma? REQUEST TEST: Vitamin B12 and Folate levels.
